Constructor for binary growth mixture models

Source: R/gmm_binary.R
binary_growth_model.Rd

Sets up the emission state for a growth mixture model of a binary outcome: each class follows its own polynomial trajectory on the logit scale, and cases vary about it through normally distributed random growth factors that are integrated out by Gauss-Hermite quadrature.

Usage

binary_growth_model(
  n_components,
  design,
  random_effects = "intercept_slope",
  psi = "equal",
  n_quadrature = 30,
  adaptive = FALSE,
  principal = TRUE,
  start_pool = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

n_components

Integer. The number of latent classes to estimate.

design

Numeric matrix with one row per occasion and one column per growth factor, as built by the polynomial in the time scores.

random_effects

Which growth factors vary within a class: "intercept_slope", "intercept" or "all".

psi

"equal", "variances" or "free", as in fit_gmm().

n_quadrature

The density of the quadrature rule: the number of nodes per random effect on the standard rule, and with two or more random effects on the principal-axis rule (principal), two thirds of this many nodes per unit of log-odds standard deviation along each axis, at least a tenth of it, and at most n_quadrature^q nodes in all.

adaptive

Logical. Keep the standard normal's nodes for every response pattern (FALSE, the default) or centre them on each pattern's posterior.

principal

Logical. With two or more random effects, lay the rule along each class's principal axes of the random effects (TRUE, the default, when adaptive is FALSE) or keep n_quadrature nodes on each standardised random effect.

start_pool

Optional list of n_components x ncol(design) trajectory matrices that half the random starts are drawn around; NULL draws every start from the pooled trajectory and the observed response patterns.

...

Additional arguments, ignored.

Value

A list object of class c("binary_growth", "emission").
